NOTICE OF 129TH ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING
NOTICE is hereby given that the 129th Annual General Meeting (‘ AGM ’) of the Shareholders of the Company will be held on 
Monday, the 27th July, 2026 at 03:00 p.m. IST through Video Conferencing (‘VC’) / Other Audio-Visual Means (‘OAVM’) to 
transact the following business:

a) the Audited Standalone Financial Statements of the Company for the financial year ended 31st March, 2026  
together with the Reports of the Board of Directors and Auditors thereon; and 
b) the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements of the Company for the financial year ended 31st March, 2026 together 
with the Report of Auditors thereon.
2. To declare dividend on equity shares of the Company for the year ended 31st March, 2026.
3. To appoint a director in place of Mr. Kumar Mangalam Birla (holding DIN: 00012813) who retires from office by rotation, 
but being eligible, offers himself for reappointment.

modification(s), the following Resolution as an Ordinary Resolution :

18. In terms of Regulation 40(1) of the SEBI Listing Regulations, as amended, securities of listed companies shall be 
transferred only in dematerialized form. Members may please note that SEBI vide its Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/
MIRSD_RTAMB/P/CIR/2022/8 dated 25th January, 2022, has mandated Listed Companies to issue securities in demat 
form only while processing service requests viz. Issue of duplicate securities certificate; claim from Unclaimed Suspense 
Account; Renewal/Exchange of securities certificate; Endorsement; Sub-division of securities certificate; Consolidation 
of securities certificates/folios; Transmission and Transposition. Accordingly, Members are requested to make service 
requests by submitting a duly filled and signed Form ISR- 4, the format of which is available on the Company’s website 
i.e. www.adityabirlarealestate.com  and on the website of the Company’s RTA i.e. www.mpms.mufg.com. It may be noted 
that any service request can be processed only after the folio is KYC compliant. Further, SEBI vide its notification dated 
24th January, 2022, has also mandated that all requests for transmission and transposition shall be processed only in 
dematerialised form. In view of the same and to eliminate all risks associated with physical shares and avail various 
benefits of dematerialisation, Members are advised to dematerialise the shares held by them in physical form. Members 
can contact the Company or RTA for assistance in this regard.

THE INSTRUCTIONS FOR MEMBERS FOR REMOTE E-VOTING AND JOINING ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING ARE AS UNDER: -
I. In compliance with the provisions of Section 108 of the Act, Rule 20 of the Companies (Management and 
Administration) Rules, 2014 as amended from time to time, and Regulation 44 of the SEBI Listing Regulations and in 
terms of SEBI Master Circular  no. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated 30th January, 2026 (Earlier 
SEBI circular no. SEBI/HO/CFD/CMD/CIR/P/2020/242 dated 9th December, 2020, in relation to e-voting facility 
provided by listed entities, read with SEBI Master Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD2/ CIR/P/2023/120 dated 11th July, 
2023 now rescinded due to issue of SEBI Master Circular dated 30th January, 2026), in order to increase the efficiency 
of the voting process, it has been decided to enable e-voting to all the demat account holders, by way of a single 
login credential, through their demat accounts/ websites of Depositories/ Depository Participants. The Company is 
pleased to provide to the members the facility to exercise their right to vote on resolutions proposed to be considered 
at the AGM, by electronic means and the business may be transacted through e-voting Services. For this purpose, the 
Company has entered into an agreement with National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL) for facilitating voting 
through electronic means, as the authorized agency. The facility of casting the votes by the members using an 
electronic voting system before the AGM (‘remote e-voting’) as well as e-voting on the date of AGM will be provided 
by NSDL.
II. The members who have cast their vote by remote e-voting prior to the AGM may also attend/participate in the AGM 
through VC/OAVM but shall not be entitled to cast their vote on such resolution again.
III. The remote e-voting period commences on Wednesday, the 22nd July, 2026 from 09:00 a.m. IST to Sunday, the  26th 
July, 2026 till 05:00 p.m. IST. During this period, Members of the Company, holding shares either in physical form or 
in dematerialized form, as on the cut-off date i.e. Monday,  the 20th July, 2026, may cast their vote by remote e-voting. 
The remote e-voting module shall be disabled by NSDL for voting thereafter. Once the vote on a resolution is cast by 
the Member, the Member shall not be allowed to change it subsequently. Those Members, who will be present in the 
AGM through VC/OAVM facility and have not cast their vote on the Resolutions by remote e-voting and are otherwise 
not barred from doing so, shall be eligible to vote through e-voting system during the AGM.
IV. The facility of joining the AGM through VC/OAVM shall open 30 minutes before the time scheduled for the AGM 
and will be available for members on first-cum-first served basis and members can join by following the procedure 
mentioned in the Notice.
V. How do I vote electronically using NSDL e-voting system?
 The way to vote electronically on NSDL e-voting system consists of “Two Steps” which are mentioned below:
STEP 1: ACCESS TO NSDL E-VOTING SYSTEM
A. Login method for e-voting and joining virtual meeting for Individual shareholders holding securities in demat mode
 In terms of SEBI Master Circular dated 30th January, 2026 on e-voting facility provided by Listed Companies, Individual 
shareholders holding securities in demat mode are allowed to vote through their demat account maintained with 
Depositories and Depository Participants. Shareholders are advised to update their mobile number and email Id in their 
demat accounts in order to access e-voting facility.

5. Password details for shareholders other than Individual shareholders are given below:
a. If you are already registered for e-voting, then you can use your existing password to login and cast your vote.
b. If you are using NSDL e-voting system for the first time, you will need to retrieve the ‘initial password’ which was 
communicated to you. Once you retrieve your ‘initial password’, you need to enter the ‘initial password’ and the 
system will force you to change your password.
c. How to retrieve your ‘initial password’?
i. If your email ID is registered in your demat account or with the company, your ‘initial password’ is 
communicated to you on your email ID. Trace the email sent to you from NSDL from your mailbox. Open 
the email and open the attachment i.e. a .pdf file. Open the .pdf file. The password to open the .pdf file is 
your 8 digit client ID for NSDL account, last 8 digits of client ID for CDSL account or folio number for shares 
held in physical form. The .pdf file contains your ‘User ID’ and your ‘initial password’.
ii. If your email ID is not registered, please follow steps mentioned below in process for those shareholders 
whose email ids are not registered.
6. If you are unable to retrieve or have not received the “Initial password” or have forgotten your password:
a) Click on “Forgot User Details/Password?”(If you are holding shares in your demat account with NSDL or CDSL)

b) “Physical User Reset Password?” (If you are holding shares in physical mode) option available on

c) If you are still unable to get the password by aforesaid two options, you can send a request at evoting@nsdl.com 
mentioning your demat account number/folio number, your PAN, your name and your registered address etc.
d) Members can also use the OTP (One Time Password) based login for casting the votes on the e-voting system

STEP 2: CAST YOUR VOTE ELECTRONICALL Y AND JOIN GENERAL MEETING ON NSDL E-VOTING SYSTEM:
 How to cast your vote electronically and join General Meeting on NSDL e-voting system?
1. After successful login at Step 1, you will be able to see all the companies “EVEN” in which you are holding shares and 
whose voting cycle and General Meeting is in active status.
2. Select “EVEN” of Company for which you wish to cast your vote during the remote e-Voting period and casting your 
vote during the General Meeting. For joining virtual meeting, you need to click on “VC/OAVM” link placed under “Join 
Meeting”.
3. Now you are ready for e-voting as the voting page opens.
4. Cast your vote by selecting appropriate options i.e. assent or dissent, verify/modify the number of shares for which 
you wish to cast your vote and click on “Submit” and also “Confirm” when prompted.
5. Upon confirmation, the message “Vote cast successfully” will be displayed. 
6. You can also take the printout of the votes cast by you by clicking on the print option on the confirmation page.
7. Once you confirm your vote on the resolution, you will not be allowed to modify your vote.
 General Guidelines for shareholders:
1. Institutional shareholders (i.e. other than individuals, HUF, NRI etc.) are required to send scanned copy (PDF/JPG 
Format) of the relevant Board Resolution/ Authority letter etc. with attested specimen signature of the duly authorized 
signatory(ies) who are authorized to vote, to the Scrutinizer by e-mail to gbgagrani@gmail.com with a copy marked 
to evoting@nsdl.com. Institutional shareholders (i.e. other than individuals, HUF, NRI etc.) can also upload their Board 
Resolution / Power of Attorney / Authority Letter etc. by clicking on “Upload Board Resolution / Authority Letter” 
displayed under “e-Voting” tab in their login.
2. It is strongly recommended not to share your password with any other person and take utmost care to keep your 
password confidential. Login to the e-voting website will be disabled upon five unsuccessful attempts to key in the 
correct password. In such an event, you will need to go through the “Forgot User Details/Password?” or “Physical 
User Reset Password?” option available on www.evoting.nsdl.com to reset the password. 
3. In case of any queries, you may refer the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) for Shareholders and e-voting user 
manual for Shareholders available at the download section of www.evoting.nsdl.com  or call on.: 022 - 4886 7000 or 
send a request to Mr. Amit Vishal, Deputy Vice President– NSDL at  evoting@nsdl.com.

Aditya Birla Real Estate LimitedANNEXURE TO THE NOTICE
I. Explanatory Statement under Section 102(1) of the Companies Act, 2013 
Item No. 4
The explanatory statement is in terms of the Regulation 36(5) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015 (SEBI Listing Regulations) as amended, however, the same is not required as per Section 102 of the 
Companies Act, 2013 (the Act).
In accordance with Section 139 of the Act read with the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014 (Rules) as amended from 
time to time, M/s. S R B C & CO. LLP (SRBC), the existing statutory auditor shall be retiring at the conclusion of the ensuing 129th 
Annual General Meeting (AGM). Therefore, based on recommendation of the Audit Committee, the Board of Directors (Board) of 
the Company at their meeting held on 6th May, 2026, have approved and recommended the appointment of M/s. Singhi & Co., 
Chartered Accountants, Mumbai, (ICAI Firm Registration No.302049E), as a statutory auditor of the Company for a first term 
of five years from the conclusion of ensuing 129th AGM to hold office till the conclusion of the 134th AGM of the Company to 
conduct the audit of accounts of the Company for the period commencing fr om FY2026-27 to FY2030-31. 
Based on the negotiations between M/s. Singhi & Co. and the Managing Director and Chief Financial Officer of the Company, 
the Audit Committee has recommended and the Board of Directors has approved, subject to the approval of the shareholders, 
an annual remuneration towards audit fees of Rs.55 lacs (Rupees Fifty Five lacs only) plus applicable taxes and out of actual 
pocket expenses and other incidental costs be paid to the auditor for the financial year ended 31st March, 2027 and thereafter 
such remuneration for the remaining tenure of the appointment as may be recommended by the Audit Committee and approved 
by the Board. The fees for services in the nature of limited review, statutory certifications and other professional work will be in 
addition to the audit fee as above and will be decided by the Board/Audit Committee in consultation with the Auditors.
Further, the Audit Committee and the Board is of the view that the above fees of Rs. 55  lacs is reasonable and deemed proper 
considering material reduction in volume of audit scope due to proposed sale and transfer of Century Pulp and Paper business 
division, as compared to the remuneration of outgoing auditor SRBC.
M/s. Singhi & Co. was founded in 1940 and is providing qualitative services since then in Assurance, Corporate Finance, 
Risk Advisory, Direct and Indirect Taxation, Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, Valuation, Forensics, ESG etc. It has its 
presence across the country including through its offices located in Kolkata, Mumbai, Noida/Delhi NCR, Bengaluru, Chennai, 
Gurgaon, Pune and Raipur. The firm is the Indian network member of Moore Global, one of the world’s leading networks of 
independently owned and managed accounting and business advisory firms, committed to provide exceptional client service.  
M/s Singhi & Co. is also registered with Public Company Accounting Oversight Boards (‘PCOAB’), USA and is a member of the 
Forum of Firms for Audit Quality.
M/s. Singhi & Co. is statutory auditors of many listed companies and provides specialised professional services across wide 
range of industries, combining with legacy of trust with deep domain knowledge and having varied sectoral footprint including 
Manufacturing, BFSI, Energy & Power, Infrastructure, Real Estate, Technology, Healthcare, Retail & FMCG, Chemicals and 
Logistics. 
M/s. Singhi & Co. is a peer reviewed firm, who meets the requirements specified in Section 141 of the Act and who have given 
their consent in writing along with a certificate of eligibility as prescribed under the Act, and that the appointment, if made, shall 
be in accordance with the applicable provisions of the Act and the Rules framed thereunder.
None of the Directors, Key Managerial Personnel and their relatives are, in any way, concerned or interested financially or 
otherwise in the resolution except to the extent of their shareholding, if any, in the Company. 
The Board accordingly recommends passing of the resolution set out at item no. 4 of this Notice for approval by the Members 
as an ordinary resolution.
Item No. 5
In pursuance of Section 148 of the Companies Act, 2013 (the Act) and Rule 14 of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 
2014, the Board is required to appoint an individual who is a Cost Accountant in Practice, or a firm of Cost Accountants in 
Practice, as Cost Auditor on the recommendations of the Audit Committee. The remuneration recommended by the Audit 
Committee shall be considered and approved by the Board of Directors and ratified by the shareholders.

Aditya Birla Real Estate Ltd. (‘ABREL’ or ‘The Company’) believes that a home is more than a 
transaction. It is a promise, shaped by trust, fulfilled through experience, and measured by the 
quality of life it creates. This year’s Integrated Annual Report is anchored in that belief and reflects 
this year’s theme: Built on Trust. Designed for Better Living.
Trust is not a claim the Company makes; it forms the foundation of everything the Company 
builds. It is earned through disciplined delivery, transparent stakeholder engagement, and an 
uncompromising commitment to quality. Every development, every partnership, and every customer 
relationship reflects the legacy and credibility of the Aditya Birla Group, a legacy built over more than 
a century.  For ABREL, trust is its most enduring asset and its most sacred responsibility.
Better Living defines the purpose behind that trust. The Company designs spaces that go beyond 
four walls to enrich the way people live, work, rest, and connect. From sustainability-led planning 
and resilient infrastructure to wellness-focused amenities and vibrant community ecosystems, 
the Company’s developments are conceived to create lasting value for residents, cities, and 
the environment.

About the  
Report
This Integrated Annual Report for 
FY 2025–26  (hereinafter referred to 
as ‘the Report’) presents ABREL’s 
holistic account of value creation 
across the short-, medium-, and 
long-term horizons. This Report 
goes beyond conventional financial 
reporting to reflect the full breadth 
of the organisation's performance, 
including strategy, governance, 
environmental stewardship, and 
social impact.
ABREL's integrated reporting 
journey is grounded in a core 
conviction: sustainable value 
creation is inseparable from 
business performance. This Report 
highlights how capital allocation 
decisions, material risks, and 
stakeholder priorities influence 
outcomes across the six capitals.
The disclosures in this Report are 
designed to serve the informational 
needs of all material stakeholders, 
including investors, customers, 
employees, regulators, and the 
communities in which ABREL 
operates. They are guided 
by transparency, balance, 
and evidence.The Integrated Annual Report for  
FY 2025–26 has been prepared in 
accordance with the International 
Integrated Reporting Framework, issued 
by the International Financial Reporting 
Standards Foundation (IFRS). The 
financial and statutory disclosures comply 
with the Companies Act, 2013, the Indian 
Accounting Standards, and SEBI (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015, including applicable 
Secretarial Standards. 
Non-financial performance is in 
accordance with the guidelines outlined 
by the Global Reporting Initiative 
(GRI) Standards (2021), and ABREL's 
sustainability initiatives are mapped to the 
United Nations Sustainable Development 
Goals (UN SDGs). The Report also 
includes the Business Responsibility and 
Sustainability Report (BRSR) for  
FY 2025–26, reflecting ABREL's 
commitment to comprehensive and  
multi-framework disclosure.This Report covers the period from  
1st April, 2025, to 31st March, 2026, and 
encompasses both financial and  
non-financial information across 
ABREL’s principal business segments: 
Real Estate (Birla Estates) and Pulp and 
Paper. The reporting scope includes 
project sites and operations across 
the Mumbai Metropolitan Region 
(Maharashtra), Bengaluru (Karnataka), 
the National Capital Region (Delhi-NCR), 
Pune, and the manufacturing facility at 
Lalkuan (Uttarakhand).
The Report focuses on topics material 
to ABREL’s operations and relevant to 
its stakeholders, including value chain 
partners, customers, and communities. 
It also provides relevant historical trends 
for context and clearly discloses any 
exclusions. ABREL publishes this Report 
annually and discloses financial results 
on a quarterly basis.

BirlaTrust is often viewed as an intangible

institution can possess.Dear Stakeholders,
In a global landscape defined by volatility, 
geopolitical tension, and accelerating 
technological change, FY 2025–26 has 
been a milestone year for the Group. Our 
large manufacturing businesses have 
consolidated their leadership positions, our 
newer ventures are scaling with conviction, 
and our legacy consumer businesses are 
being reshaped for a new era of growth. 
Across this diverse portfolio, one force 
continues to anchor our progress—trust.
Trust is often viewed as an intangible asset. 
In reality, it is one of the most consequential 
forms of capital an institution can possess. 
In periods of uncertainty, markets can 
turn volatile and competitive advantages 
can erode. Trust, however, compounds. It 
enables organisations to make long-term 
investments when others hesitate, to 
navigate disruption with credibility, and to 
emerge stronger from periods of change.
For a group such as ours, trust extends 
far beyond the relationship between a 
company and its customers. It is reflected 
in the confidence of shareholders who 
support long-term value creation, the 
commitment of employees who choose 
to build their careers with us, the faith of 
partners and suppliers who invest alongside 
us, and the confidence of communities and 
governments that see us as a responsible 
participant in economic progress. Each of 
these constituencies grants an institution 
something invaluable: the licence to grow.
This is particularly relevant at a time when 
businesses are being asked to do more 
than deliver financial performance. They 
are expected to navigate technological 
disruption, manage increasingly complex 
supply chains, create meaningful 
employment, steward natural resources 
responsibly and contribute to social 
progress. Meeting these expectations 
requires more than scale or strategy. It 
requires credibility built over years and, in 
many cases, decades.
The strength of our portfolio today reflects 
the cumulative effect of that credibility. It 
has allowed us to invest through cycles, 
pursue transformation with confidence and 
attract talent, capital, and partnerships that 
strengthen our competitive position.

Global Economy in 2025
The global economy maintained its 
trajectory through 2025 despite elevated 
tariffs, policy uncertainty, and geopolitical 
tensions. The impact of tariff measures was 
less severe than projections had suggested, 
and growth across major economies 
remained broadly stable.
World trade expanded faster than 
anticipated in 2025, as demand for AI-driven 
capex offset the effects of trade policy 
uncertainty and higher tariffs. The volume 
of world merchandise trade grew by 4.6%, 
compared to a forecast of 2.4%. For the 
second consecutive year, Asian economies 
were the largest contributors to total world 
trade volume growth, accounting for 3.2 
percentage points of the 4.6% total—or 71% 
of the overall increase.
Trade in 2025 was also supported by 
investment in AI infrastructure, demand 
in emerging markets, fiscal and monetary 
expansion in advanced economies, and 
frontloading of imports in North America 
ahead of anticipated ‘reciprocal’ tariffs from 
the United States. The outbreak of conflict 
in the Middle East on 28th February, 2026, 
along with the partial closure of the Strait of 
Hormuz and damage to energy production 
facilities, introduced a supply shock to the 
global economy.
India in FY 2025–26: Domestic 
Demand Carries the Economy 
Forward
Against a challenging global backdrop 
marked by US tariff escalations and 
mounting trade policy uncertainty, the 
Indian economy demonstrated remarkable 
resilience during FY 2025–26. Real GDP 
growth accelerated to 7.6 %, up from 7.1% 
in FY 2024–25, cementing India’s position as 
the fastest-growing major economy globally. 
This performance was underpinned by 
robust domestic demand, low inflation, and 
a broad pro-growth reform agenda. On the 
demand side, private consumption grew 
7.7% year-on-year, supported by income tax 
reductions and rationalisation of GST rates. 
Economic activity was broad-based. On 
the supply side, manufacturing gained 
momentum, driven by the automobile and 
fast-moving consumer goods sectors. The 
services sector benefited from demand in 
retail trade, hospitality, transportation, and 
real estate. India also made progress in containing inflation, with the headline rate 
averaging 2% in FY 2025–26, down from 
4.7% the previous year. 
India’s economic prospects for FY 2026–27 
carry both opportunities and risks. Growth is 
projected at 6.6% by RBI, marginally revised 
down due to the effects of the Middle East 
conflict, which has pushed up global energy 
prices and disrupted shipping through 
the Strait of Hormuz. India nonetheless 
remains among the fastest-growing major 
economies globally.
Private consumption is expected to remain 
the primary driver of growth, though elevated 
global oil prices are likely to feed into 
domestic inflationary pressures. The GST 
rate reductions introduced in September 
2025 are expected to partially offset 
this impact. Investment is projected to 
continue, supported by government capital 
expenditure, improved trade access through 
recently concluded free trade agreements, 
and a stable financial sector. 
India’s macroeconomic position, including 
foreign exchange reserves, a narrowing 
current account, and a path of fiscal 
consolidation, provides some buffer against 
external shocks. The pace of the renewable 
energy transition, the credibility of fiscal 
policy, and the implementation of newly 
concluded trade agreements will be factors 
that determine the trajectory of growth in the 
coming years.
Aditya Birla Group: In Our People 
We Trust
At the Aditya Birla Group, trust is built 
through experience. It is earned in 
thousands of everyday interactions—when 
people are given opportunities to learn, 
when careers progress on merit, when 
leaders are accessible, when commitments 
are honoured, and when employees know 
they can depend on the organisation through 
moments that matter.
Over time, these experiences shape how 
people feel about the Group. They influence 
whether talented individuals choose to join 
us, whether they see a future with us, and 
whether they are willing to invest their energy 
and ambition here over the long term.
The progress we have made across 
talent, leadership, culture and employee 
experience during the year reflects this 
enduring focus.A Sharper Identity, a Clearer 
Purpose
This year also marked the completion of a long 
journey of focus. With the divestment of the 
Pulp and Paper business to ITC Ltd., ABREL is 
now, unambiguously, a real estate company. 
This clarity strengthens capital allocation, 
undivided management attention, and a 
balance sheet structure aligned with the long 
real estate cycle. 
Trust in Competence: Helping 
People Succeed from Day One
The employee experience begins long before 
an individual settles into a role. The quality 
of hiring, onboarding and early support 
often shapes how quickly people become 
effective and how confidently they navigate a 
new environment.
During the year, we onboarded more than 
11,700 employees, including over 80 senior 
leaders, across businesses and functions. 
Structured hiring and onboarding processes, 
clear communication and timely feedback 
helped create a stronger experience for 
candidates and new joiners alike.
We also continued to simplify the day-to-day 
employee experience through technology. 
Mobile-first onboarding and AI-enabled 
platforms such as AVA, which recorded more 
than 7,00,000 interactions during the year, 
improved accessibility, and delivered greater 
consistency at scale.
Capability building remains central to  
long-term success. Employees are more likely 
to perform with confidence when they have 
access to the skills, knowledge and support 
required to succeed. Through Gyanodaya, 
our Global Centre for Leadership Training, and 
other business-led  initiatives, we delivered 
more than 280 programmes, reaching over 
8,500 employees across technical, functional, 
behavioural and leadership domains. 98% of

through the Gyanodaya Virtual Campus (GVC). 
In addition, an intense 3-month group-wide 
learning initiative, the ‘Learning Fest’, engaged 
more than 39,000 employees, a fourfold 
increase over the previous year.
Managers play a critical role in shaping this 
experience. Through coaching, feedback and 
day-to-day guidance, they influence how 
employees learn, grow and navigate their 
careers. We therefore continue to invest in 
strengthening leadership capability across

Trust in Growth: Building Careers 
across the Group
The strength of an organisation is often 
reflected in the opportunities it creates for 
its people. During the year, more than 6,400 
employees moved across roles, functions, 
businesses or geographies. This is, by all 
accounts, a very significant number. These 
movements reflect the scale and diversity 
of opportunities available across the Group 
and reinforce our promise of A World 
of Opportunities.
Internal mobility also provides an important 
measure of organisational confidence. Of 
the 6,400+ movements during the year, 
more than 470 were across businesses. At 
senior leadership levels, cross-business 
mobility accounted for 15% of movements, 
strengthening leadership depth across the 
portfolio. Nearly 69% of senior management 
roles were filled through internal hiring, 
reflecting the quality and readiness 
of leadership talent developed within 
the Group.
These outcomes are supported by a 
disciplined approach to identifying and 
developing talent. 27% of employees form 
part of the Group Talent Pool. We have also 
built a strong pipeline of future leaders.
Our ability to attract high-quality talent 
continues to reflect the strength of our 
employer brand. Diversity hiring stood at 
19% during the year, while retail businesses 
achieved 40% women hiring. Women’s 
representation within the leadership cadre 
increased by 8%. Seventy-four per cent of 
new hires were below the age of 35, with 
Gen Z accounting for 39% of all new joiners. 
The Group also received recognition across 
leading platforms including LinkedIn, the 
Top Employers Institute, Forbes and the 
Financial Times.
Trust in Care: Supporting People 
and Families
The employee experience extends beyond 
the workplace. Health, wellbeing and 
support systems influence how people feel, 
perform and engage over the long term.
Through our health, wellbeing and insurance 
initiatives, we supported employees and 
their families in meaningful ways. During the 
year, more than 8,600 counselling sessions 
were availed by employees, while workmen 
and staff accessed a further 3,100+ sessions, reflecting growing awareness and 
acceptance of mental wellbeing support. 
In parallel, over 3,400 eligible employees 
underwent annual health check-ups, 
reinforcing our focus on preventive care.
These efforts are translating into measurable 
outcomes. Among Mumbai-based 
employees, the proportion of individuals in 
the high-risk category, in terms of health, 
declined from 21% to 10%, while the low-
risk category increased from 48% to 56%.
Employee sentiment continues to reflect this 
strong foundation. In our Annual employee 
survey, Vibes 2026, 96% of employees 
expressed pride in being part of the Group, 
90% said they would recommend us as a 
great place to work, and 93% reported that 
their business inspires them to do their best 
work every day.
Trust in Purpose: Extending 
Impact beyond the Workplace
Employees increasingly seek a sense of 
contribution that extends beyond their 
immediate roles. The Group’s social

may never meet. Such acts speak to a 
shared belief in the purpose and impact of 
these initiatives.
Ultimately, the strongest measure of 
trust is behaviour. It is reflected in the 
choices people make, to join the Group, to 
pursue opportunities across businesses 
and geographies, to take on larger 
responsibilities, and to build long-term 
careers within the organisation. It can 
be seen in the strength of our leadership 
pipeline, the mobility of our talent, the 
quality of our employee experience and the 
pride employees express in being associated 
with the Group.These outcomes are built gradually through 
consistent actions and shared experiences. 
They create continuity through periods of 
growth and change and provide a strong 
foundation for the future.
The Company’s Performance
In an evolving real estate landscape, 
trust has emerged as the sector’s most 
enduring differentiator. As the Indian 
real estate market continues to mature, 
homebuyers are increasingly placing their 
trust in developers who combine quality, 
transparency, execution excellence, 
and long-term credibility. This shift is 
reshaping the sector and accelerating 
the consolidation of demand in favour of 
organised and established players.
India’s real estate sector continues to 
demonstrate remarkable resilience. 
Supported by rapid urbanisation, 
infrastructure-led development, rising 
aspirations, and a growing preference for 
premium living, the sector remains an 
important pillar of India’s long-term growth 
story. Although overall sales volumes across 
major cities witnessed some moderation, 
total sales value increased, supported by 
sustained demand for higher-value homes 
and steady price appreciation across key 
micro-markets. While FY 2025–26 witnessed 
intermittent global uncertainties and 
phases of cautious consumer sentiment, 
the underlying fundamentals of the market 
remained firmly intact.
Against this backdrop, Aditya Birla Real 
Estate delivered a year of strong operational 
and strategic progress. The trust placed in 
us by our customers translated into Birla 
Estates achieving its highest-ever annual 
booking value and collections during  
FY 2025–26, with bookings of

marked an entry into the Thane market, 
further strengthening presence in the

What the Reported Numbers 
Reflect
I would like to begin by addressing an issue 
that merits clear and direct explanation. 
In FY 2025–26, ABREL’s reported financial 
results did not fully reflect the underlying 
strength of the Company’s financial position 
and operating performance.
Under Ind AS accounting standards, 
which are aligned with global IFRS norms, 
revenue in real estate is recognised only 
upon project handover—not at the time of 
booking, collection or during the tenure of 
project execution. Accordingly, customer 
payments received during construction 
are recorded as liabilities on the balance 
sheet until possession is handed over. As a 
result, strong operational performance and 
subdued reported revenues can, and often 
do, coexist.
The divestment of Pulp and Paper business 
was announced in March 2025. Accordingly, 
its results are shown as discontinued 
operations in the financial statements.
During FY 2025–26, in the absence of 
significant project handovers during the 
year, reported revenues declined on a Keyur ShahUnder Ind AS 115, real estate revenues are 
recognised at the point of project handover rather 
than when bookings are signed or collections are 
received.

A Legacy of Excellence,    
A Future of  Innovation: 
Mission, Vision  
and Values
For over 125 years, ABREL has embodied resilience, evolution, and leadership. Founded in 
1897 as a textile enterprise, the Company has steadily transformed into a dynamic, diversified 
organisation with a strong presence in Real Estate and Pulp and Paper.
Built on a foundation of trust, innovation, and a deep commitment to stakeholders, ABREL 
continues to drive industry progress, elevate customer experiences, and contribute meaningfully 
to society. As part of the Aditya Birla Group (ABG), the Company embraces a philosophy of 
purpose-led growth, prioritising sustainability, excellence, and forward-thinking solutions.
In the Real Estate sector, ABREL reimagines urban living through its LifeDesigned® philosophy, 
creating spaces tailored to contemporary lifestyles. In the Pulp and Paper segment, the 
Company focuses on operational efficiency and environmental stewardship to deliver 
sustainable, high-quality products. 
Across all its businesses, ABREL is guided by a clear Mission and Vision, ensuring that every 
initiative aligns with long-term aspirations and responsible growth.

A Road Map of Legacy
Birla Estates Pvt. Ltd. (referred to as ‘Birla 
Estates’ or ‘BEPL’), a wholly owned subsidiary 
of Aditya Birla Real Estate Ltd. (ABREL), is the 
real estate venture of the Aditya Birla Group. 
In 2016, Birla Estates was established with 
the philosophy of LifeDesigned® homes and 
office spaces. BEPL’s mission is to transform 
the Indian real estate sector by creating value 
and providing an unparalleled experience for all 
stakeholders. In a short span, the Company has 
positioned itself as a trusted and premium real 
estate brand, delivering high-quality residential 
and commercial developments across key urban 
markets including MMR, Bengaluru, Delhi-NCR, 
and Pune.
The residential projects of BEPL are thoughtfully 
planned to enhance urban living with integrated 
green spaces, wellness features, and lifestyle 
amenities. Landmark projects such as Birla 
Niyaara in Mumbai exemplify its premium 
offerings. On the commercial front, Birla Estates 
owns and operates two Grade A office buildings 
in Worli, Mumbai, offering ~6.1 lakh sq. ft. of 
leasable area, designed to balance business 
efficiency and employee well-being.
Vision
We will transform the perception of the Indian 
real estate sector by delivering an exceptional 
experience and creating value, at every level, for 
every stakeholder.Mission  
We will provide an iconic brand experience 
aligned to our legacy by never compromising 
on transparency, commitment, quality and 
superior design.Our Business Verticals
ABREL thrives on its diverse business 
segments, including Real Estate and Pulp 
and Paper. In Real Estate, the Company 
creates spaces that inspire and endure, 
transcending mere structures. The Pulp and 
Paper division is committed to sustainable 
practices, manufacturing materials that 
set new benchmarks for environmental 
responsibility. Together, these varied segments 
highlight ABREL’s adaptability and resilience, 
positioning the Company as a dynamic entity 
capable of meeting the diverse demands of 
different industries while upholding a strong 
commitment to excellence.

Located in the scenic region of 
Lalkuan, Uttarakhand, the Pulp 
and Paper segment, Century Pulp 
and Paper, is a leading industry 
figure. Since 1984, this segment 
has been recognised for producing 
premium writing and printing paper, 
packaging board, green pulp, and 
tissue products. As the largest 
manufacturer of paper, board, 
tissue, and pulp from a single 
location in India, the division has 
also made a significant mark in the 
global export market. With service 
centres, sales offices nationwide,

ensure a seamless experience for

Reading the Year Right: Operational 
Momentum and Reported Financials
FY 2025–26 was a year in which ABREL’s financial statements and its 
financial health told meaningfully different stories. Under Ind AS 115, 
and global IFRS norms, real estate revenues are recognised only at 
project handover, rather than at booking or collection. Consequently, 
customer payments received during the construction phase continue 
to remain on the balance sheet as advances until possession is 
transferred. As a result, strong operational performance and weak 
reported revenues can coexist within the same fiscal year.
Three data points when viewed together, provide a more complete 
picture of the year’s performance. First, BEPL sustained a booking 
value of ` 8,136 Crores against a base year that itself doubled over 
the previous year. This performance was achieved in an operating 
environment where sales volumes declined across most Tier-1 cities. 
Second, collections increased 23.5% year-on-year to  
` 3,341  Crores, while maintaining strong collection efficiency holding at 
99%. Third, consolidated revenue from continuing operations declined 
to ` 403.77 Crores from ` 1,203.37 Crores in FY 2024–25, primarily 
due to the absence of major handover-led revenue recognition events 
during the year.
These outcomes are not contradictory; rather, they are precisely what 
the accounting standard prescribes for a developer mid-pipeline. The 
` 3,342 Crores collected during the year will translate into recognised 
revenue progressively as ongoing projects reach completion 
milestones over the next 24 to 36 months. Further strengthening this 
visibility, launched projects alone carry an estimated surplus cash flow 
potential of approximately ` 9,637 Crores.Completing the Transition: A Singular Real 
Estate Identity
The defining strategic event of the year was the completion of ABREL’s 
transition to a focused real estate enterprise. Following the divestment 
of the Textiles division in FY 2024–25 , the Company executed a 
Business Transfer Agreement with ITC Limited on 31st March, 2025, 
for the sale of the Pulp and Paper undertaking, structured as a slump 
sale for an aggregate consideration of ` 3,498 Crores. Conditions 
precedent under the agreement are in advanced stages of satisfaction, 
and the transaction is expected to close in the near term. Pulp and 
Paper assets and associated liabilities are presented as held for sale in 
the FY 2025-26 financial statements, with assets of ` 3,041 Crores and 
directly associated liabilities of ` 401.69 Crores classified accordingly 
under Ind AS 105.
This strategic transition marks a significant sharpening of the 
Company’s long-term focus. ABREL now allocates capital, 
management attention, and organisational energy to one business 
line in which it has demonstrated leadership: premium and luxury 
residential development under the Birla Estates brand, alongside a 
high-quality leased commercial portfolio.
The anticipated receipt of the Pulp and Paper divestment is expected 
to further strengthen the Company’s financial position. It will reduce 
reliance on borrowings, strengthen the consolidated balance sheet, 
and unlock additional resources for project acquisitions and execution 
across core markets.
FY 2025–26 was a year in which 
ABREL’s financial statements and its 
financial health told meaningfully 
different stories. Under Ind AS 115, 
and global IFRS norms, real estate 
revenues are recognised only at 
project handover, rather than at 
booking or collection.

Performance Overview, Standalone
On a standalone basis, ABREL recorded Total Income from continuing 
operations of ` 516.23 Crores compared to ` 497.60 Crores in  
FY 2024–25, a 3.7% increase. Profit before tax from continuing 
operations increased significantly to ` 121.38 Crores from  
` 0.06 Crores in the prior year, driven by improved operating leverage 
and substantially lower exceptional charges. Profit after tax from 
continuing operations stood at ` 128.64 Crores, marking a turnaround 
from a loss of 15.05 Crores in FY 2024–25.
Net profit from discontinued operations stood at ` 223.25 Crores 
against a loss of ` 8.70 Crores in FY 2024–25. This performance 
reflects the orderly transition of the Pulp and Paper business and the 
recognition of profit on transfer of property, plant, and equipment. 
Performance Overview: Consolidated
The consolidated performance reflects the developer-stage 
characteristics of the ABG’s real estate operations. Consolidated 
revenue from continuing operations stood at ` 403.77 Crores 
compared with ` 1,203.37 Crores in FY 2024–25. The decline is driven 
by the timing of project completions under Ind AS 115, rather than 
any weakening in underlying demand or commercial momentum. It is 
aligned with a pipeline that continues to progress on schedule but has 
not yet reached its handover-weighted years.Consequently, total net profit for the year stood at ` 351.89 Crores, 
compared with a net loss of ` 23.75 Crores in FY 2024–25.
The Company’s standalone net worth strengthened to ` 4,692.88 
Crores from ` 4,376.77 Crores, supported by retained earnings and 
the reversal of net deferred tax liability of ` 123.76 Crores following the 
Company’s decision to opt for the new tax regime from FY 2026–27. 
Operating margin (including discontinued operations) improved 
to 5.80% from 2.91% in FY 2024–25, and net profit margin after 
exceptional items improved to 10.47% from a negative 0.67%.
Total income from continuing operations was ` 459.16 Crores against

operations stood at ` 338.07 Crores against ` 148.74 Crores in 
FY 2024–25. After accounting for profit of 223.25 Crores from 
discontinued operations, the consolidated net loss for the year was

institutional partnerships, reinforcing Birla Estates’ position as a 
preferred India real estate partner for global institutional capital.

standards, and execution credibility.

institutional capital into the Group’s real estate platform. This 
reduced reliance on conventional borrowings and validated the 
institutional readiness of the Birla Estates platform.

the year. The standalone debt-equity ratio stood at 0.89, broadly in

operating profitability.

to provide a materially stronger foundation for the Company’s 
growth ambitions. Liquidity remained healthy during the year, with

through digital dashboards, providing real-time visibility on  
project-level cash flows. Moreover, all projects launched during the

Working Capital and Inventory Build-up
The growth in consolidated inventory increased from 4,726 Crores in 
FY 2023–24 to 11,060 Crores in FY 2025–26, a 134% expansion over 
two years. This increase was driven by the Company’s accelerated 
land acquisition and project ramp-up strategy. As projects remain 
under development, contracted future revenue continues to be 
reflected as inventory on the balance sheet until revenue recognition 
is triggered upon project completion under Ind AS 115.
The Company funded this inventory build-up through a combination 
of customer collections, internal accruals, and calibrated borrowing. 
Consolidated borrowings increased from ` 2,502 Crores at the close 
of FY 2023–24 to ` 5,636 Crores at the close of FY 2025–26. In line 
with this, working capital expanded from ` 1,997 Crores to  
` 6,441 Crores. 
Over the next 24 to 36 months, this trajectory will reverse as ongoing 
projects reach handover. This transition will convert inventory into 
recognised sales and cash, while supporting the deleveraging path to 
which the Company has committed to.
Investor Engagement and Market 
Performance
The Company’s share price during the year reflected the 
transition discount that markets typically apply to companies 
mid-  transformation. The stock closed FY 2025–26 at  
` 1,123.00 against ` 1,959.90 at the close of FY 2024–25, 
representing a decline of 42.7%. Market capitalisation 
correspondingly declined from ` 21,891 Crores to ` 12,543 Crores. 
This movement must be read in two contexts. First, the Nifty Realty 
index underperformed the Nifty 50 by 26 percentage points in CY 
2025, indicating a sector-wide  
correction that affected listed real estate broadly. Second, the 
residual gap reflects the window that opens between operational 
performance and reported P&L during a developer’s mid- pipeline phase.
 Notwithstanding the FY 2025–26 movement, the Company’s  
three-year share price CAGR stood at 21.0% from ` 634.00 on  
31st March, 2023, to ` 1,123.00 on 31st March, 2026, and the  
five-year CAGR stood at 19.3% from ` 465.05 on 31st March, 2021, 
both reflecting the longer-arc value created through the Company’s 
strategic transformation.
The Company maintained continuous engagement with investors 
and analyst throughout the year, comprising quarterly earnings calls, 
strategic roadshows in key financial markets, and participation in 
industry conferences. It also engaged with independent investor 
relations agencies to conduct regular market perception studies, 
with insights informing the Company’s communication strategy and 
reinforcing transparency. The Company also incorporated actionable 
feedback into its messaging frameworks to address investor concerns 
proactively and reinforce confidence in the Company’s long-term 
growth plans.
The Board has recommended a dividend of ` 2.50 per equity 
share of face value 10 each, equivalent to 25% on paid-up equity 
share capital, against ` 2.00 per share (20%) in the prior year. The recommendation, subject to shareholder approval at the 129th Annual 
General Meeting, reflects confidence in underlying cash generation 
and the visibility of revenue conversion ahead.
Governance, Ethics, and Responsible 
Financial Management
Financial performance was underpinned by a strengthening 
governance framework. The Control Effectiveness Index (CEI) 
improved to 88–89 during the year against a target of 90-plus. This 
improvement was driven by greater process automation, real-time 
monitoring, and remediation of identified control gaps. The Enterprise 
Risk Management framework continues to be enhanced to capture 
real estate-specific execution risks, macroeconomic sensitivities, 
and emerging exposures including climate transition. The Company 
also strengthened its data governance frameworks to align with the 
Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, ensuring readiness for 
regulatory commencement.
The audit of Standalone and Consolidated Financial Results for the 
year ended 31st March, 2026, was conducted by SRBC & Co LLP 
(ICAI Firm Registration Number 324982E/E300003), who issued an 
unmodified audit opinion. The Board, at its meeting held on 06th May 
2026, approved and recommended the appointment of M/s. Singhi & 
Co. (ICAI Firm Registration Number 302049E) as Statutory Auditors 
for a term of five consecutive years from the conclusion of the 129th 
AGM, covering FY 2026–27 to FY 2030–31. The transition follows 
completion of SRBC & Co LLP’s second five-year term and is in 
compliance with the rotation requirements under Section 139 of the 
Companies Act, 2013, subject to shareholder approval.
ABREL did not record any incidents of corruption, regulatory

Party Transactions Policy continue to govern conduct across the 
organisation, with periodic training and certification reinforcing

Tax Strategy
ABREL’s tax governance framework is overseen by the Finance 
Committee with active participation from the Audit Committee. The 
Company operates exclusively within the Indian tax jurisdiction and 
discharges all direct and indirect tax obligations in full compliance 
with applicable laws. Standard Operating Procedures for both 
direct and indirect taxes ensure timely and accurate compliance. In 
addition, practising chartered accountants issue monthly compliance 
certifications to validate the integrity of tax reporting processes.
During the year, the Company evaluated the implications of 
amendments under the Income Tax Act, 2025, as amended by the 
Finance Act, 2026. After assessing the new tax regime introduced 
from Tax Year 2026–27, the Company elected to opt for the new 
regime, resulting in the reversal of net deferred tax liability of  
` 123.76 Crores on account of lower applicable tax rates, recognised 
under Tax Expense in the Statement of Profit and Loss.
ABREL refrains from seeking or accepting undue government 
incentives or tax holidays. The Company includes all tax disclosures 
in its audited financial reports, which are independently assured by 
statutory auditors. This provides stakeholders with full visibility into 
the Company’s tax positions and practices.
Cost Management and Operating Efficiency
Cost discipline remains foundational to the Company’s operating 
model. The Real Estate business operates on a scalable outsourced 
execution model, engaging only Grade-A contractors and vendors 
under tight internal supervision. Cost benchmarking, design efficiency 
reviews, and value engineering are institutionalised across all major 
projects, allowing the Company to manage material procurement 
costs and optimise project timelines without compromising on the 
premium positioning of Birla Estates developments.
Working capital management remained tight through the year. 
Inventory increased to ` 11,060.48 Crores on a consolidated basis, 
reflecting deliberate land and project investment to support the 
future revenue pipeline. This was complemented by a substantially 
improved cash from operations position of ` 747.23 Crores, 
demonstrating that growth investment was funded primarily by 
internal accruals and customer collections rather than incremental 
external borrowings.
Sustainability-aligned Capital Allocation
A material portion of capital deployment during FY 2025–26 was 
directed towards sustainability-aligned outcomes, reflecting 
the Company’s commitment to the ABG’s Net Zero by 2050 
ambition. The Company continued to design projects to globally 
recognised standards, including LEED Platinum, IGBC, and BREEAM 
certifications. During the year, it formally adopted BREEAM for its 
more rigorous water conservation requirements, a priority area in the 
Indian context.
The 140 KW solar plant commissioned at Birla Centurion delivered 
168,000 kWh of power in its first operational year, avoiding 
approximately 114 metric tonnes of CO2 emissions. Birla Niyaara remains India’s first LEED pre-certified residential building, and Birla 
Aurora has achieved Net Zero Energy status. 
ABREL was recognised as the Regional Sector Leader and Global 
Sector Leader for Non-listed Companies in Asia in the 2025 GRESB 
Real Estate Assessment Development Benchmark, one of the 
most authoritative global benchmarks for real estate sustainability 
performance. The Company was also recognised among India’s Top 
60 Most Sustainable Companies by Business World, securing the 
second position in the Real Estate and REITs sector.
These achievements reflect a deliberate principle: sustainability 
investment is treated not as a cost overlay but as a value driver that 
protects long-term financial returns through lower operating costs, 
stronger asset values, and enhanced institutional investor preference.
Way Forward
ABREL enters FY 2026–27 as a focused, well-capitalised, pure-play 
real estate enterprise. The strategic foundation is firmly in place: a 
single-business identity, an ` 73,858 Crores GDV pipeline across  
34.7 million sq. ft., a deepening institutional partner base, and a 
balance sheet on the cusp of materially strengthening once Pulp and 
Paper proceeds are received.
Three priorities will shape capital allocation in the coming year. First is 
continued investment in land acquisition and project launches in core 
markets where the Birla Estates brand premium is most pronounced, 
with NCR, MMR, Bengaluru, and Pune anchoring the residential 
pipeline. 
Second, is the systematic deleveraging of the consolidated balance 
sheet, with debt-to-equity expected to fall below 1.0 post-divestment 
proceeds. Third, is the progressive conversion of contracted bookings 
and collections into recognised revenue, which will close the gap 
between operational performance and reported financial results over 
the next 24–36 months.
The Company is not building for the next quarter. It is building for the 
decades ahead.Corporate Overview  Statutory Reports  Financial Statements

Trust:   
The Foundation of ABREL’s Capital
In Real Estate, what we build matters, but why people trust us 
matters more. It is what a family places in us when they invest 
their life’s savings in a home. It is what an enterprise signals when 
it leases space for its people. Every asset we create, every space 
we deliver, is a direct expression of that trust and that is what our 
manufactured capital, at its core, represents.
For ABREL, trust is not built through marketing. It is earned through 
every development decision. It is reflected in the design integrity, 
structure durability, process transparency, timeline honesty 
and the measurable performance of assets across its entire life. 
LifeDesigned® articulates that trust into tangible, lasting places. Manufactured capital measures and report it, serving as both the 
evidence of the promise and a record of accountability.
In FY 2025–26, every square foot of manufactured capital was shaped 
to earn, honour and deepen trust. This trust was expressed through the 
LifeDesigned® philosophy and delivered through quality, transparency

LifeDesigned®: The Architecture of Trust
LifeDesigned® is ABREL’s promise to understand, nurture and enrich 
the everyday lives of the people in its developments. It integrates 
innovation, craftsmanship and purpose across scales, from individual 
homes to master plans. At its core is a simple intent: to create 
spaces that serve people who live and work in them, now and across 
generations. 
This philosophy shapes decisions across the development lifecycle, 
from master planning and material selection to construction methods, 
digital engagement and long-term asset management. In practice, it 
translates into architecture that enhances functionality and integrates natural light and ventilation. It also includes ample green areas that 
promote well-being, curated amenities for diverse lifestyles and smart 
home technology that improves convenience and energy efficiency.
At the heart of LifeDesigned® is the Nature, Culture and Architecture 
framework, a design discipline that ensures every ABREL development 
responds to its natural surroundings, reflects its cultural context and 
expresses architectural integrity. This approach ensures that every 
space is planned not only for immediate functionality and comfort, but 
also for enduring value.

One Intellectual Capital Architecture 
Standing on Eight  Pillars
At ABREL, intellectual capital extends beyond boardroom strategy. It 
is embedded in every cubic metre of concrete poured, every sensor 
reading captured, every window tested, and every mason trained 
on-site. The Company’s Intellectual Capital Architecture functions as 
a living, site-level ecosystem built on eight interconnected innovation 
pillars. These pillars span the full development lifecycle, from design 
conceptualisation to the physical realities of construction, materials, 
and knowledge transfer.
Where the industry typically treats innovation as episodic, the real 
estate business engineered a systemic architecture where design is 
the genesis point. It is where customer intelligence, cultural context, 
environmental sensitivity, and lifestyle foresight converge to shape developmental decisions. The remaining seven pillars govern how 
projects are executed.
Technology informs process, processes generate data, data drives 
quality assurance, quality assurance feeds back into knowledge 
management. In turn, knowledge management shapes the next 
cycle of material and supply chain decisions. This creates a circular, 
compounding intellectual capital, where every project site is 
simultaneously a beneficiary and a contributor, and where every pour, 
test, and training session makes the entire organisation smarter.
The eight pillars below are not isolated silos. They are interconnected layers of a single system, visible on every real estate division’s 
construction site, from foundation to finishing.Systemic Architecture: Circular Compounding Intellectual Capital

LifeDesigned® is ABREL’s proprietary philosophy that 
goes beyond aesthetics to function as a scalable design 
knowledge system. It integrates human behaviour,

development approach, ensuring that each project

Nature–Culture–Architecture (NCA): A Structured Design Logic
Architecture emerges from a sensitive understanding of both nature and culture, acting as a mediator between the environment and human life. Nature–Culture–Architecture (NCA): A Structured 
Design Logic
NCA serves as a structured design framework that 
integrates environmental sensitivity, local culture, and 
built form. By embedding this framework early in the 
design process, ABREL creates developments that 
respond to their surroundings while remaining timeless 
and adaptable.Insight-led Design Tools

Challenge:  In high-rise construction, what 
happens beneath the ground is invisible but 
critical. Earth pressure on deep basements, 
load distribution across raft foundations, 
and actual in-situ concrete strength cannot 
be assessed through visual inspection or 
traditional testing alone. Decisions about 
when to strip formwork, when to load the next 
floor, or when to verify foundation performance 
have historically relied on conservative 
assumptions rather than real-time data.Monitor earth pressure on deep basements and 
diaphragm walls to ensure excavation does not overstress 
the retaining system.1
Verify load transfer to foundations/raft by measuring 
actual pressure on soil or rock, helping detect uneven 
settlement risks.2
Improve safety during deep excavation by giving early 
warning of rising lateral pressure on retaining walls.3
Assess stress changes around underground structures 
such as parking, basements, and utility tunnels 
below towers.4

Pillar 8: Supply Chain and Material Management Innovation
Fostering Innovation in the Pulp and 
Paper SegmentExtending quality control upstream 
to the factory and downstream to the 
point of placement, ensuring zero-defect 
material flow.
A structured SOP for Material Evaluation governs the identification and 
approval of acceptable brands and suppliers based on defined quality requirements. The process includes material testing through both  
in-house and external laboratories.
Quality at the real estate division begins at the manufacturer’s factory 
floor, not at the site gate. At project site, materials are stored per 
approved protocols with batch-wise segregation, moisture protection, 
and traceable identification. And at the point of use, every concrete 
truck is tested and documented, while teams reject non-conforming 
loads outright. This reflects an end-to-end material quality 
governance, from source to structure. 
Since 1984, innovation has been central to the Pulp and Paper 
business, driving product development, process efficiency, 
and sustainable solutions. This focus is guided by three pillars - 
sustainability, quality, and cost efficiency, and strengthened through 
continued investment in R&D, upgraded technical capabilities, and a 
dedicated innovation team to expand market presence and support 
new product development.

Occupational Health and Safety
Health and safety are non-negotiable priorities at ABREL. The Company 
operates a strong Occupational Health and Safety Management System 
aligned with ISO 45001:2018, reinforcing its commitment to protecting 
employees, workers, and on-ground teams across operations.
ABREL embeds safety into everyday work through clear procedures,  
on-site controls, and continuous training. Regular safety drills, 
emergency preparedness programmes, and hands-on demonstrations 
strengthen awareness and readiness across project sites and 
operational facilities.
The Company supports employee well-being through comprehensive 
insurance coverage, including medical, life, and personal 
accident protection.
ABREL manages operational risks through defined Standard Operating 
Procedures, permit-to-work systems, and frequent audits. In addition, 
the OHSMS framework covers all workers, including those at project 
sites and labour camps. 
Risk assessments, toolbox talks, incident reporting, and escalation 
mechanisms reinforce ABREL’s Zero Harm commitment. The Company 
closely monitors safety performance and links it to leadership accountability, driving a culture of vigilance, responsibility, and 
continuous improvement. Upholding Human Rights
Our real estate division is committed to conducting business responsibly and upholding fundamental human rights across its 
operations. The Company seeks to protect the dignity, safety, and rights of employees, communities, contractors, and supply chain 
partners at every stage of its business activities.
To reinforce this commitment, the Company has established a comprehensive Human Rights Policy aligned with internationally 
recognised frameworks. The policy guides ethical conduct, responsible decision-making, and respect for human dignity. It also 
supports sustainable development and encourages responsible stakeholder engagement.
The Company further integrates human rights principles into its governance and operational practices through oversight, due diligence, 
and risk mitigation processes. It works proactively to prevent human rights violations and maintains formal grievance mechanisms to 
address concerns in a timely and transparent manner, ensuring accountability and fair resolution for affected stakeholders.

Customer Experience and Satisfaction 
Earning Trust at Every Square Foot
The LifeDesigned® philosophy and its execution framework, NCA: 
Nature-Culture-Architecture, forms the foundation of BEPL’s 
design approach.
The Real Estate division’s core purpose is ‘To Enrich Lives by Building 
Happy Communities that are Rooted in Trust’. Through LifeDesigned®, 
the Company translates this purpose into thoughtfully crafted 
spaces that understand, nurture and enrich lives, while shaping the 
communities they serve. 
The NCA framework operates across three integrated pillars:
•  Nature:  Every site undergoes a formal biodiversity, microclimate, 
and comfort study. The Real Estate division targets a perceptible 
temperature reduction of 8–10°C within the site boundary through 
strategic landscaping, water bodies, and shade design across its 
projects. The Company plants a minimum of 80% native species 
to support local biodiversity and reduce water dependency. 
At Birla Punya, Sangamwadi, biodiversity strategies include 
dedicated Nectar Zones and Larva Hosting Zones. Meanwhile 
at Birla Trimaya, a man-made lake regulates microclimate and 
creates a living landscape.
•  Culture:  The Real Estate division conducted 52 culture surveys 
across 16 contexts and 29 cities. The surveys mapped local 
festivals, solar orientation traditions, community gathering 
patterns, and cultural identity markers, directly informing 
the architectural character, amenity design, and landscape 
programming at each project. 
•  Architecture:  At Birla Arika, solar study and festival integration 
shape the architectural experience. The LifeDesigned® Philosophy, Where Trust Begins in Design 
120ADITYA BIRLA REAL ESTATE LTD.
The Customer Journey, Backed by Digital 
Excellence
The Real Estate division further strengthened the home-buying journey 
through transparency, speed, and consistent communication.  
In FY 2025–26, it made significant investments in digitising 
and streamlining the customer lifecycle, from initial inquiry to 
unit handover.
The most transformative initiative was the full migration of the 
customer lifecycle onto a global top CRM platform, consolidating 
various legacy IT systems into a single, integrated platform. This 
created a unified source of information for customer-related data 
and reduced customer onboarding TAT by up to 77.5% by eliminating 
manual interventions across multiple touchpoints. The platform also 
improved visibility across 31 additional post-purchase steps, enabling 
proactive communication and faster resolution. All CRM, sales, and 
marketing team members were trained and onboarded.
Complementing this, the Real Estate division further deployed an 
in-house AI Voice Analytics Tool, developed in collaboration with the 
Group’s Analytics team, to evaluate the quality of every customer 
service call. The tool assesses key parameters including discussion 
themes, customer sentiment, relationship manager tone, empathy, 
knowledge depth, and conversation fluidity. Between August 2025 
and March 2026, approximately 15,000+ calls were analysed, and 
performance scores were shared with team leads to support coaching 
and continuous improvement in customer handling quality. 
The QC App, launched in May 2025, digitised quality management at 
construction sites, enabling structured inspections, real-time issue 
reporting, and traceable Non-Conformance Report (NCR) closure 
with direct management visibility. This strengthened the link between 
construction quality and customer experience at possession. 
The Real Estate division’s Real Advice platform continues to serve as a 
homebuyer education initiative that simplifies complex topics such as 
TDS obligations, property transfer procedures, home loan structures, 
and legal documentation in an accessible, expert-led format. The 
platform, amplified through Vicky Kaushal as brand ambassador, 
helps prospective buyers make informed financial decisions with 
improved confidence.Measuring Trust, NPS, CSAT and Complaint 
Resolution 
The most honest measure of customer trust is the score a customer 
gives when no one is watching. The Real Estate division has 
invested in a strong, multi-touchpoint measurement framework that 
independently verifies customer satisfaction, tracks it systematically, 
and links it directly to action.
In FY 2025–26, the division expanded its Net Promoter Score (NPS) 
framework to four touchpoints across the homebuyer lifecycle, 
with plans to extend it further to six touchpoints by the end of the 
fiscal year:

clarity, speed, and transparency of documentation and legal handover 
procedures. The Waiting Period score of 65 remains an acknowledged 
area of focus, with the Customer Council prioritising more frequent 
communication and stronger digital engagement.
The Customer Council, chaired by the CEO and comprising the 
Deputy CEO, heads of Sales, Marketing, CRM, Operations, Facility 
Management, and Regional Heads, meets monthly to review Voice of 
the Customer (VoC) insights, identify satisfaction drivers, and prioritise 
improvements. During the year, the Council implemented design 
standardisation and targeted experience upgrades across project 
cycles. 
For the commercial portfolio, the annual Customer Satisfaction 
Survey across Birla Aurora and Birla Centurion recorded an overall 
CSAT rating of 98%. This reflects consistently high standards of facility 
management, responsiveness, and tenant experience across both 
properties.

directly or indirectly. Across both the business divisions, community 
well-being is treated as a structured social investment rather than a 
compliance requirement. Programmes are built around defined focus 
areas, community-owned prioritisation, and measurable outcomes.

Community Programmes and Their Impacts in 
Lalkuan 
Pulp and Paper’s community engagement is rooted in the geography

Social Forestry
Social Forestry is one of the Pulp and Paper division’s flagship 
programmes through which plantation activities are carried out on 
several thousand hectares and several hundred nurseries across 13 
districts in Uttarakhand. During FY 2025-26, plantation reached an 
all-time high of 2.2 Crore saplings, and the goal is to reach 2.5 Crore 
saplings by FY 2027-28. This initiative created green cover, supported 
biodiversity conservation, improved soil health, prevented erosion, and sustained water conservation. It also provided raw material security for 
the manufacturing operations in a sustainable, long-term cycle. 
The Pine Leaf Initiative, One Programme,  
Three Outcomes
Every summer pine trees in the Himalayan foothills shed their leaves. 
If left unmanaged, these dry leaves become a serious fire hazard. The 
Pulp and Paper division has entered a formal MoU with the Forest 
Division to address this risk through a community-linked solution. 
Under this initiative, local women are engaged to collect fallen 
pine leaves (Perul) from the hillsides, preventing forest fires, while 
generating direct livelihood income for women in rural households. 
The division in turn uses the collected biomass as boiler fuel, reducing 
its dependence on coal. This single programme delivers three 
measurable outcomes: environmental protection, women’s economic 
empowerment, and industrial decarbonisation. During the first half of 
the fiscal year, approximately 435 MT of Perul was collected.At the Pulp and Paper division, the Occupational Health Centre 
‘PEHEL’, managed through dedicated software, provides free OPD, 
IPD, and medicines to employees, their dependents, workers and 
members of the surrounding community. Extending this support 
further, free ambulance services are also available to outsiders. 
The Pulp and Paper division also strengthens access to specialised 
treatment through hospital tie-ups in Haldwani and Rudrapur, while 
periodic multi-speciality camps broaden healthcare outreach. Blood 
donation camps and targeted medical awareness programmes for girls 
and women in the surrounding community further extend the health 
commitment beyond the plant gates.

Responsible Supply Chain and Procurement  
ABREL’s Values, All the Way Down the Chain
A company’s values are only as real as the supply chain they travel through. At ABREL, responsible procurement is a commitment, not a 
procurement policy.
Responsible and Green Procurement
The Real Estate division developed a structured Critical Supplier 
Identification Methodology to map its supplier base of 1,241 vendors 
and identify 30 critical suppliers, accounting for approximately 80% 
of procurement value. These suppliers are segmented by ESG risk, 
material versus service category, and regional concentration. It also 
plans desk-based assessments and on-site assessments across 
identified critical suppliers, covering environmental compliance, 
labour standards, occupational safety, and governance practices.
In parallel, the division has also implemented a Green Supply Chain 
Management policy with ESG onboarding criteria embedded into 
supplier registration. It also runs a capacity-building programme 
for the top 60+ suppliers. In addition, all vendor contracts include 
explicit Health & Safety obligations, ensuring that BEPL's zero-harm 
commitment extends across all on-site contractors.
On sustainable materials, the division’s NCR projects demonstrates 
that responsible sourcing and cost efficiency can go hand in hand.
At Birla Navya, Gurugram, recycled content reached 22.07% against 
20% target, achieved through the use of Recycled Concrete Aggregate 
(RCA) and Recycled Aggregate (RA) pavers derived from C&D waste, in 
alignment with IS 383 standards. Local material sourcing also reached 
80%. 
Additionally, a formal tie-up with the Municipal Corporation Gurugram 
(MCG) enabled structured C&D waste disposal. This generated a cost 
savings of ` 325 per cubic metre and eliminated the use of 3,000 cubic 
metres of virgin material in PCC works. At one project in the Delhi NCR 
region, the Company reused all C&D waste within the site boundary, 
eliminating the need to send any waste outside the premises.On procurement spend, across both divisions, 87% of the total 
procurement was done from within India while 2.05% of total 
procurement budget was spent on MSMEs/Small Producers. 
The Bandhu digital tendering platform introduced transparency and 
procurement efficiency into BEPL's procurement processes, reducing 
bid evaluation time by approximately 70% through automated bid 
comparison and structured audit trails.

Assessing Climate Risks to Safeguard 
Natural Capital and Build Resilient Assets
The truest measure of trust in real 
estate is whether a building will still 
stand physically, financially, and 
environmentally, decades from now. 
Climate risk assessment is how we 
provide that assurance.
Climate change continues to reshape how organisations engage with 
the natural environment, affecting access to water, energy systems, 
land use, and broader ecological stability. For a real estate developer 
like ABREL, the long-term viability of these resources is critical. As 
a result, climate-related risks have become immediate design and 
planning priorities rather than distant future concerns.
Within ABREL’s Real Estate division, climate risk assessments form 
a core component of the environmental strategy and sustainability 
governance framework. These assessments identify potential 
vulnerabilities across the built environment and the surrounding 
natural ecosystems, enabling informed decision-making across 
site selection, design, material use, and operational planning. 
They also evaluate physical risks such as flooding, heat waves, 
and water stress, alongside transition risks stemming from 
evolving climate regulations, market expectations, and global 
decarbonisation pathways.
Approach to Climate Risk Assessments
Physical climate risk assessments are conducted using the IPCC’s 
Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs), which model plausible 
climate futures under different mitigation levels. The assessments 
follow a six-step methodology: Data Collection, Climate Scenario 
Modelling, Identification of Major Risks, Assessing Adaptive Capacity,

decarbonisation across the full value chain.Embodied Carbon Assessment
Reducing Embodied Carbon in Construction
Embodied carbon, the greenhouse gas emissions arising from the 
manufacture, transport, and installation of construction materials, 
forms a significant and often underestimated share of a building’s 
total lifecycle carbon footprint. For a real estate developer, addressing 
embodied carbon is therefore as critical as improving operational 
energy efficiency. ABREL has systematically advanced this agenda 
during the year, by expanding its programme from early-stage 
assessment at a single project to full portfolio coverage.
Scope and Approach
Embodied carbon assessments catalogue major construction 
categories, incorporate emission factors from trusted industry 
databases including ICE (Inventory of Carbon and Energy) and 
Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs), and automatically 
compute total embodied carbon per project. The assessments cover 
lifecycle stages A1 to A5, including cradle-to-gate emissions for all 
materials (A1-A3), as well as transportation and installation emissions 
from the manufacturing source to construction site (A4-A5).
The system boundary includes the Core and Shell (C&S) scope 
and energy consumed during construction site operations. C&S 
comprise structural and primary building elements such as concrete, 
reinforcement steel, masonry, and base plaster. These components 
are common across projects, minimally influenced by tenant-specific 
variations, and account for the majority of material-related emissions. 
As a result, this boundary enables consistent benchmarking of 
embodied carbon intensity across projects and reporting periods. 
The Company is also working to expand the boundary to include MEP 
components in future phases.

Energy Mix: Scaling Renewables, Shrinking Fossil 
Fuels
The Real Estate division continues to rely primarily on grid electricity, 
supplemented by on-site solar and solar-powered lighting at 
worker camps. Diesel and CNG remain limited to vehicles, backup

decline as grid connectivity and solar provisioning expand.
The Pulp and Paper division operates a more complex energy

operations, together with Perul (seasonal biomass) and Compressed 
Methane Gas (CMG) from bio-methanation, form the core of the 
energy mix. Meanwhile, reliance on non-renewable fuels including 
diesel, coal, furnace oil, LPG, LSHS continues to recede as biomass 
substitution accelerates.

Water Performance
In FY 2025–26, total water withdrawal stood at 1,14,05,174.06 kL, reflecting a 1.36% change YoY. Groundwater remained the dominant source, 
accounting for ~98%, followed by third-party and treated water at 2.07%. The Company did not withdraw water from surface bodies.
*The TDS of water withdrawn is below 1000 mg/l The Pulp and Paper division operates in a naturally favourable groundwater-recharge region. However, the scale of industrial withdrawal demands 
active stewardship. The business therefore invests in internal recycling, Kaizen-led process innovation, and tertiary treatment to ensure that 
operational efficiency does not come at the cost of aquifer health.
